nnue.title: Engine strength (NNUE)
nnue.description: NNUE judges quiet positions far better than the classical evaluator it replaces — on a rook endgame it reports +3.77 where classical reports +0.53. It needs a 40 MB network file, downloaded once per device the first time the engine runs and then cached permanently. Turn it off to avoid that download on a metered connection; analysis then falls back to the weaker classical evaluator. Stored per device.
nnue.applies: Takes effect the next time the engine starts.

workers.title: Engine workers
workers.description: How many Stockfish processes analyse a game in parallel. More is faster until you run out of memory, and then it is dramatically slower — measured on a 12-core / 8 GB laptop at depth 18, 4 workers took 9.7 s, 6 took 7.6 s, and 8 took two minutes because it started swapping. Auto stays conservative because the browser reports total memory, never free memory, so it cannot know your headroom. Raise it if analysis feels slow and your machine has RAM to spare; lower it if the fans annoy you. Stored per device.
workers.applies: Takes effect on the next analysis.
workers.slowBuildTitle: Analysis is running ~11× slower than it should
workers.slowBuild: This page is not cross-origin isolated, so Stockfish fell back to its single-threaded build. Measured on the same game at depth 18: 9.7 s threaded versus 110 s single-threaded. The fast build needs the COOP and COEP headers from public/_headers to reach the browser — check that they are deployed and that no proxy is stripping them.

freePlayStrength.title: Play vs engine — default strength
freePlayStrength.description: Used when you click "Play it out vs engine" after finishing a practice line. Maximum is full-strength Stockfish. The lower levels handicap the engine via UCI_LimitStrength + Skill Level so you can pressure-test a line at a more human level. You can override this per-session on the practice page itself.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: Chess Coach is a personal chess analysis tool you run in your browser. We've kept the privacy story short on purpose: there is no Chess Coach backend that stores your data, no analytics, no advertising tracking, and no third-party data sharing.
privacy.localData: <bold>Locally in your browser (IndexedDB):</bold> the games you import, the engine evaluations Chess Coach computes for them, your repertoire trees, and which library puzzles you have solved. On most accounts this data stays on the device that produced it. The puzzle library itself is a public dataset shipped with the app — downloading it tells us nothing about you.
privacy.auth: <bold>Authentication:</bold> we use Clerk to sign you in. Clerk holds your email address and any OAuth identifiers (Google, GitHub) you choose to link. See <link>Clerk's privacy policy</link> for what they store about you.
privacy.profileSync: Profile sync (Supabase): we mirror a tiny "profile row" (your Clerk user id and your Chess.com username) to Supabase so different devices can recognise the same account. Game data and analyses are not synced — they live in IndexedDB on whichever device produced them.
privacy.cloudSync: Cloud sync (Supabase), off by default: for specifically enabled accounts, Chess Coach also mirrors imported games, their engine analyses, and puzzle results to Supabase so they survive a cleared browser and reach your other devices. It is not on for an account unless it has been added to an allowlist in the database, and the database refuses the writes otherwise. When it is on, the Settings page shows a Cloud sync card with the last run and a manual trigger. Nothing is shared with anyone else either way.
privacy.extSyncStorage: In chrome.storage.sync: your Chess.com username, the URL of your Chess Coach app, and a boolean toggle for whether to show the after-game prompt. Nothing else.
privacy.extSees: What the extension sees: only the URL and DOM of chess.com tabs (it has no permission for any other site by default). When you click "Test connection" in the options page, it will request one-time permission to fetch your configured Chess Coach URL — granted per-host with your explicit consent.
privacy.extSends: <bold>What the extension sends:</bold> nothing, anywhere, ever. The deep link it builds is a URL navigation in your own browser; no data leaves your machine via the extension.
privacy.noAnalytics: No analytics, tracking pixels, or session-replay tools.
privacy.noSelling: No selling, renting, or sharing your information with third parties.
privacy.noChessReading: No reading of your chess.com account beyond the public game archive you opt into via username — Chess Coach uses Chess.com's public API and never asks for your password.
privacy.deleteDesc: Use Settings → Reset (or the browser's "Clear site data" devtool) to wipe IndexedDB. To remove the Supabase profile row, sign out of Clerk and email the address below. The extension's stored settings can be cleared by removing the extension from chrome://extensions.
privacy.contactDesc: Questions about this policy or about a deletion request: open an issue on the Chess Coach repository, or reach out via the email listed on the Chrome Web Store listing for this extension.

explain.missedMate: There was a forced mate available — the engine sees a winning sequence that ends the game.
explain.allowedMate: This move walks into a forced mate — the opponent now has a sequence that ends the game.
explain.missedFork: A move was available that attacks two valuable pieces at once, so the opponent can't save both.
explain.missedPin: A piece could have been pinned against a more valuable one, freezing it in place.
explain.missedSkewer: A line attack on a valuable piece would have forced it to move, exposing the piece behind it.
explain.missedBackRank: The opponent's back rank was weak — a heavy piece could have delivered (or threatened) mate along the first/eighth rank.
explain.fork: The opponent's reply attacks two of your pieces at once, and you can't save both.
explain.pin: Your piece is now pinned to a more valuable piece behind it — it can't move without losing material.
explain.skewer: A line attack now forces a valuable piece of yours to move, losing the piece behind it.
explain.backRank: Your king is stuck on the back rank with no escape squares — heavy pieces can mate along the first/eighth rank.
explain.hangingPiece: A piece is left undefended, attacked by more pieces than defend it. The opponent can take it for free.
explain.trappedPiece: A piece has no safe squares to move to — it will be lost on the next move.
explain.overloadedDefender: A defender is asked to do too many jobs at once — protecting it on one front leaves another open.
explain.discoveredAttack: Moving one piece uncovers an attack from a piece behind it.
explain.weakKing: Your king has lost its pawn cover and several attackers are converging — the position is unsafe.
explain.lostMaterial: The line ends with you down material — pieces drop without sufficient compensation.
explain.other: A significant evaluation drop without a clean tactical name attached.

cloud.title: In the cloud
cloud.empty: Nothing uploaded yet — run a sync.
cloud.hint: Counts only, a few hundred bytes per read. Advances while the server-side analysis worker runs; refreshes itself about once a minute until the library is fully analyzed with NNUE.

sync.title: Cloud sync
sync.description: Backs up your reviewed games, their engine analyses, and your puzzle progress to Supabase, so they survive a cleared browser and follow you to another device.
sync.archiveNote: The cloud copy only ever grows — deleting a game here does not remove it there, and a later sync brings it back. That is what makes it a backup; prune from the Supabase dashboard if you ever need to.
